scope: M4.1 hardening only: TrustStore concurrency safety, real wire-level replay evidence, rekey semantics, failure-safe rotation, revocation window, lifecycle CLI, exact fleet verification. No benchmark, M5 not started.

truststore_concurrency.problem: fileStore.Lookup read s.peers without a lock while Replace/Reload swapped the whole map under the write lock; the returned Peer also aliased the registry's mutable slices
truststore_concurrency.fix: Lookup takes RLock and returns a defensive copy (SignPublic, AgreementPublic, SM2UserID, RetiredKeyIDs cloned); Replace stores a copy and releases its lock with defer; IDs/Revision/Reload lock discipline reviewed
truststore_concurrency.tests: TestLookupReturnsADefensiveCopy, TestPeerCloneIsolation, TestConcurrentLookupWithReload, TestConcurrentLookupWithReplace, TestConcurrentRevocationAndLookup, TestConcurrentRotationAndLookup

wire_level_replay.problem: the M4 replay test only called Send on a closed channel; it never delivered session A's real ciphertext to session B
wire_level_replay.fix: a relay captures the exact ProtectedRecord frames (length prefix + version + kind + SM4-GCM ciphertext) session A produced; they are injected byte-for-byte into session B's connection after B's handshake
wire_level_replay.result: rejected at the record layer, no business side effect

cross_device_ciphertext.problem: the M4 test proved business identity binding, not ciphertext isolation
cross_device_ciphertext.fix: genuine ciphertext from D001 is injected into D002's session and vice versa
cross_device_ciphertext.result: rejected in both directions at the record layer; the business-binding test is retained

rekey_semantics.problem: Device.Run ran MaxSessions sessions unconditionally, so a device with MaxSessions>1 disconnected and re-handshaked even when the policy had not fired
rekey_semantics.fix: MaxSessions is only a ceiling; a second handshake happens only when Rekey.Due() is true at a transaction boundary
rekey_semantics.counting_rule: every ProtectedRecord successfully written or read counts one; one telemetry->control->ACK transaction is therefore 3 records on the device side; the counter is examined only at transaction boundaries, so no control is ever left pending
rekey_semantics.tests: TestNoRekeyBeforeThreshold (1 session, 0 rekey events, 9 records), TestRekeyStillFiresWhenDue (3 sessions, 3 distinct SIDs)

rotation_failure_safety.problem: the M4 rotation deleted the old key files before writing the new ones, so a mid-way failure left the device without a usable private key while the registry still named the old generation
rotation_failure_safety.fix: key files are now named by KEY ID (keys/<device>/<key-id>.key) so two generations coexist; the order is write+verify new files, atomically commit the registry, then retire old files best effort
rotation_failure_safety.atomicity_statement: the registry commit is atomic; the whole key-file+registry rotation is failure-safe, NOT crash-atomic

revocation_window.problem: Gateway.serve ignored the error from the post-handshake TrustStore lookup
revocation_window.fix: a lookup or lifecycle failure closes the channel, refuses to register the session, and emits a session-registry rejection

commands: secctl status (rewritten for the current reality)

fleet_verifier.exact_accounting: --expect-sessions makes session, telemetry and control counts exact rather than lower bounds
fleet_verifier.result: 20 devices, 60 sessions, 180 telemetry expected and accepted, 180 controls confirmed, 17/17 checks

bugs_found_by_the_new_tests: Lookup had no lock and aliased registry slices
Unregister deleted unconditionally, so a superseded session's cleanup could remove the NEW session
Register refused a reconnecting device instead of superseding the stale session
a pre-M4 device had KeyGeneration 0, so the first rotation derived key ids that were already in use
the rekey early-stop path fell into a default branch that dereferenced a nil error
the fleet threshold/sample relationship was undocumented (threshold 4 truncated a 3-sample session)
verification_gaps: the race detector still cannot run on this machine (MinGW requests __iob_func, absent from msvcrt.dll); the concurrency tests added here are functional, NOT race-detector results
SM2 key agreement still has no independent implementation cross-check (OpenSSL exposes no SM2MQV)
reuse of an ML-KEM encapsulation key across sessions is not detectable by the responder
not_claimed: a post-quantum secure system (SM2 identity authentication is not post-quantum)
a security audit or compliance certification
may_proceed_note: M4.1 is complete. The two verification gaps are carried forward and must be closed before deployment or any claim of complete verification.
